messages.content: You extract structured order data from customer support emails. Reply with a single JSON object that validates against the JSON schema given in the user message. Use null for any field the email does not state; never guess. Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currencies as ISO 4217 codes, and amounts as plain numbers with a dot as the decimal separator. Keep names exactly as written. The email may be in any language. Do not wrap the JSON in markdown and do not add any commentary. The email is provided as raw headers plus body. The From header contains the customer's name and email; the Date header gives the order date when the body does not state one explicitly. The To header is always support@helphub.example and must never be used for customer_email. Extract order_id, total_amount, and currency only from the customer's own words in the body; ignore numbers that appear in other contexts.

JSON schema:
{"properties": {"order_id": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated", "title": "Order Id"}, "customer_name": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Full name of the customer as written", "title": "Customer Name"}, "customer_email": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Customer's email address", "title": "Customer Email"}, "order_date": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated", "title": "Order Date"}, "total_amount": {"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order total as a plain number, no symbol", "title": "Total Amount"}, "currency": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR", "title": "Currency"}, "issue": {"enum": ["damaged", "missing_item", "wrong_item", "late_delivery", "billing_error", "other"], "title": "Issue", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id", "customer_name", "customer_email", "order_date", "total_amount", "currency", "issue"], "title": "OrderFields", "type": "object"}

Email:
From: María José García <kwame65@example.de>
To: support@helphub.example
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 14:22:11 +0200
Subject: Order - late delivery??

Hello support team

I am writing because my order still not here. It was supposed to come last week on the 11th but nothing. I check tracking and it says delayed in customs since 10th April. This is very bad because I need the items for my mothers birthday on 25th.

The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025. My name is María José García and email kwame65@example.de. I dont have the order number handy because the confirmation email went to spam and I deleted it by mistake. 

Please can you check with the shipping company? I want it delivered ASAP or I will need a refund.

Also I saw on your website it says 2-3 business days delivery but it has been 6 days now. This is not acceptable.

Thanks
María

P.S. I tried calling your phone number but it just rings and rings. No one answers.

message.reasoning:
We need to output JSON matching schema. Fields:

order_id: Not mentioned (no order number). So null.
customer_name: As written: "María José García". Should keep exact case/spelling.
customer_email: From header: kwame65@example.de . Also repeated in body same. Use that.
order_date: Need order date. Body states: "The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025." That seems like payment date maybe also order date? But we should use explicit statement about order date. There's mention: "It was supposed to come last week on the 11th but nothing." That refers to expected delivery date, not order date. They say they don't have order number. The Date header is Wed, 16 Apr 2025 which could be considered order date if not stated elsewhere. However there is an explicit date in body: "on 16/04/2025" associated with total amount. Could treat that as order date? Usually order date might be separate. Since they gave date of payment, likely order placed then. We'll take order_date = 2025-04-16 (YYYY-MM-DD).
total_amount: 424.49 (plain number)
currency: JPY (ISO 4217)
issue: Based on description: "my order still not here... delayed in customs ... late delivery". Issue type enum includes "late_delivery". So issue = "late_delivery".

Check required fields all present.

Now produce JSON without markdown.
